title: Runtime env overrides: BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_BE_BUN reach the packaged executable
description: Found while delivering WCLI-16 (measured on bun 1.3.14, macOS arm64). The executable built with --no-compile-autoload-dotenv/bunfig ignores the working directory's bunfig.toml and .env, but two inherited environment variables are still honoured by the embedded runtime before any Ward code runs: (1) BUN_OPTIONS="--preload ./x.ts" preloads arbitrary code into the ward process; (2) BUN_BE_BUN=1 turns the executable into the full bun CLI, which runs arbitrary scripts (-e) under Ward's executable identity and loads the working directory's bunfig.toml again. A check inside Ward cannot close (1), because the preload runs first and can remove the variable. No bun build flag disables either. Spec §4.2 already disclaims arbitrary code with equivalent authority, so the open question is not severity but binding: if WCLI-3 binds the vault key's keychain ACL to the ward executable's code identity, (2) makes that binding hollow, since any code can run as that executable. Needs a decision under WCLI-3 (opum-doc) before code: accept and document, launch through a small native launcher that scrubs the environment, or choose a runtime without these switches.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision recorded in opum-doc states whether the packaged executable must resist BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_BE_BUN, with the measurement it rests on
If it must: a test runs the packaged executable with BUN_OPTIONS preloading a marker-writing file and with BUN_BE_BUN=1 -e, and neither runs code; the same test against the WCLI-16 executable fails
If it need not: SECURITY.md or the threat-model doc names both variables as a stated limitation

implementationNotes: Sibling found in the WCLI-5 review, 2026-09-28: @napi-rs/keyring loads any module named by NAPI_RS_NATIVE_LIBRARY_PATH in place of its native binding. Measured: a compiled probe loaded a harmless planted module. Unlike BUN_OPTIONS and BUN_BE_BUN, the binding reads this variable only when it is first imported, after src/cli/guard.ts has run. The guard now deletes the variable, and a compiled test with an unguarded control shows the override loading only without the guard. It is closed, not merely accepted.
